lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with the basics: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're asking about your son Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now I need to ask: **Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand your situation better.

**Do you contribute financially or in other ways (such as food, clothes, or pocket money) towards Alex's upkeep? And if so, how much do you contribute?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help with things like clothes and other bits and pieces for him. I give about £10 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help assess your eligibility, I need to know a bit more about the timing.

**How long has Alex been living away from you? Has it been more than 8 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been living away for a few months now, yes, more than 8 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. 

Since Alex has been living away for more than 8 weeks, the amount you contribute becomes important. You mentioned you contribute about £10 a week.

To continue receiving Child Benefit when your child lives elsewhere for more than 8 weeks, you generally need to contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment itself. Currently, Child Benefit is £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child, and £16.95 per week for additional children.

**Would you be able to increase your contributions to at least match the Child Benefit rate (£25.60 per week for Alex as your only/eldest child), or is £10 per week the amount you're able to contribute?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: £10 a week is what I'm able to contribute at the moment. That's all I can manage right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about your circumstances. I understand that £10 per week is what you're able to manage.

Just to complete my assessment, I need to ask: **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex (for example, the person he's living with)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if anyone else is claiming for him or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you would **not be eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

- Alex is 8 years old, which meets the age requirement (children under 16 qualify)
- You live in the UK, which meets the residence requirement
- However, Alex has been living away from you for more than 8 weeks

When a child lives with someone else for more than 8 weeks, you can still receive Child Benefit, but only if you contribute towards their upkeep by at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment itself. For an eldest or only child, that's £25.60 per week.

You mentioned you're contributing £10 per week towards Alex's clothes and other items, which is unfortunately less than the £25.60 per week threshold needed to maintain eligibility.

**What this means:** The person who Alex is living with would likely be the one entitled to claim Child Benefit for him, as they are the ones primarily responsible for his day-to-day care.

I understand this may not be the answer you were hoping for, especially given that you are contributing what you can towards Alex's upkeep. If your circumstances change and you're able to increase your contributions to at least £25.60 per week, or if Alex comes back to live with you, your eligibility could change.

Therefore, the claimant does not meet the contribution requirement to continue receiving Child Benefit for Alex who has been living elsewhere for more than 8 weeks.
